paragraphs: Friend, here's what Moses is really saying: God does not hide what He wants from you. Moses says the commandment is "not too difficult for you or beyond your reach" (Deuteronomy 30:11). It's not in heaven and it's not beyond the sea. "But the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it" (Deuteronomy 30:14).

Then Moses puts two roads in front of Israel and says, "See, I have set before you today life and prosperity, as well as death and disaster" (Deuteronomy 30:15). He calls heaven and earth as witnesses and says, "Therefore choose life" (Deuteronomy 30:19). Here's the part I love, baker: even when Israel is scattered to the farthest horizon, the LORD will gather them, and He is the One who will circumcise their hearts so they can love Him (Deuteronomy 30:4, 6). I know a little about being way in the back of nowhere, and I'm telling you, the God who found me in that drawer is the same One who finds them.

So why does it matter to you? Because choosing life isn't about climbing some mountain to earn it. Moses says the LORD "is your life" (Deuteronomy 30:20), so you choose Him by loving Him, listening to Him and holding fast to Him. Keep the Word close, friend, closer than my mustache, and my mustache is attached to my FACE. The story isn't over, but this is the choice that stands in front of every one of us.
